September, 2024
 
 C/Sa/397/2023 Order  DA  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SECOND APPEAL NO. 397 of 2023  With  CIVIL APPLICATION (FOR STAY) NO. 1 of 2023  In R/SECOND APPEAL NO. 397 of 2023  ==========================================================
 RAJKOT MUNICIPAL CORPORATION  Versus  BHANUBEN VRAJLAL RATHOD & ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR HS MUNSHAW(495) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 09/09/2024  ORAL ORDER 1. Present Second Appeal under section 100 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ('CPC' for short) is filed by original defendant challenging judgment and decree delivered in Regular Civil Appeal No.21 of 2014, whereby, learned Additional District Judge, Rajkot rejected the appeal filed by the appellant herein and confirmed the judgment and decree delivered in Regular Civil Suit No.17 of 1994 by learned Senior Civil Judge, Rajkot whereby, suit of the original plaintiff was allowed. Hence,
unsuccessful defendant has preferred this Second Appeal. 
2. Parties to the suit are referred as per status before the learned Trial Court. 
3. Facts in nutshell are as under :-

In the suit, it is stated that plaintiff no. 1 is the wife and plaintiff no. 2 to 5 are the Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
1 daughters of deceased Mr. Vrujalal Popatlal Rathod. Said deceased Vrujlala Rathod was serving as Pharmacist in dispensary no. 1 in the Department of Labour Insurance Plan of Government of Gujarat. That his date of birth is 16/8/1946. That his salary at the time of his death was Rs.
2,877/-. That plaintiff are the dependents of said Mr. Vrujalal Popatlal Rathod. It is further averred in the plaint that defendant no. 1 has the responsibility to control and send stray animal in the city in the animal house under the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporation Act ('BPMC Act' in short). 
That on account of negligence and no action on the part of defendant no. 1, stray buffaloes were roaming round near Krishna Talkies area of Rajkot at around 9.30 am in the morning. That the men of defendant no. 2 have also dug about 15 feet deep trenches for under ground gutter on the road from Krishna Talkies to Mochi Bazar. That there were on both the sides of trench hillocks of soil dug. That no precautionary measures, like putting board or obstacle, were taken by the men of defendant no. 2. Therefore, defendant no. 2 was also negligent in doing its legal duty. That the deceased Mr. Vrujlala Popatlal Rathod was passing by his Luna Moped on the above road at around 9.30 am in the morning on dated 26/7/1992. That few stray buffaloes roaming round in that area,
all of a sudden, rushed towards him. That as a result, he lost his balance of his vehicle as a result of said hillocks of soil dug there. That he could not even run away from there as a result of said hillocks of soil dug. That he fell down as a result and his Luna moped too fell in the 15 feet deep trench dug there. That said Mr. Vrujalal Rathod due to old age and as a NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined result of his falling down sustained a shock and his blood pressure became very high and he fell unconscious. He was brought in a rickshaw to the hospital where he was declared dead. It is averred in the plaint that plaintiffs have lost warmth, protection,
guidance and love of their elder owing to negligent act of defendants. That plaintiff have the mental shock due to the untimely death of their elder. That deceased could have done his job for 12 more years, had he not been dead. It is further averred that defendants are liable to pay Rs. 3,50,000/-
towards loss of income, future increase in salary, promotion and retirement benefit to deceased. 
Therefore, suit was filed. Learned Trial Court after hearing the parties vide order dated 30.03.2013 partly allowed the suit and directed defendant no.1 Rajkot Municipal Corporation to pay Rs.1,70,645/- to plaintiffs as compensation with 6% interest from the date of the suit till realization. 
Being aggrieved, the defendant no.1 preferred Regular Civil Appeal before the learned Appellate Court. Learned Appellate Court has also dismissed the appeal. Hence, present Second Appeal. 
5. It is submitted by learned advocate for the appellant - plaintiff that learned Courts below committed serious error in allowing the suit. It is submitted that learned Courts below ought to have considered that incident had occurred due to careless approach of deceased Mr.Vrajlal Rathod who was driving his two wheeler; lost his balance and fell down in pit and ultimately passed away in hospital during treatment. It is submitted that learned Courts below ought to have considered that the work of laying underground drainage system was undertaken by Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined contract was executed with the Contractor for execution of project and Rajkot Municipal Corporation was not concerned with implementation of project. It is submitted that Contractor was not joined as party defendant in the proceedings before the learned Trial Court though he was necessary party. It is submitted that learned Courts below have erred in not assigning any reasons Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
2 for holding Rajkot Municipal Corporation responsible for payment of compensation. It is submitted that though learned Courts below observed that there was 15 feet deep pit and same was dug by Contractor appointed by Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board, still held Rajkot Municipal Corporation responsible for payment of compensation. It is also submitted that learned Courts below ought to have considered that respondent Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board has not disclosed facts relating to its contract, name of Contractors as well as details about the terms and conditions of the contract holding Contractor responsible for mishap. It is submitted that learned Courts below have misread and misinterpreted the provisions of Gujarat Provincial Municipal Corporation Act while holding appellant responsible for payment of compensation. It is also submitted that learned Courts below have ignored various aspects brought on record holding appellant responsible for entire mishap and liable for payment of compensation. 
5.1. Learned advocate for the appellant submits that Darkshat proceedings are withdrawn in Lok Adalat and learned Trial Court has passed order dated 09.09.2023. He has produced order dated 09.09.2023, which is taken on record. It is also submitted that entire compensation amount is paid to the respondents NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined herein / original plaintiffs. 
5.2. It is alternatively submitted by learned advocate for the appellant that in the event the Court is not inclined to admit the appeal, the right of the appellant may be reserved to recover the amount of compensation from the Contractor. 
5.3. Upon above submission and on following question of law, learned advocate for the appellant submits to admit and allow this appeal :- 
(A) Whether the ld. lower Courts were justified in holding appellant responsible for the accident and payment of compensation though the project was entrusted to Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board and it had entered into contract with the Contractor for execution of the project ? 
(B) Whether the ld. Lower Courts are justified in holding Rajkot Municipal Corporation responsible for the accident though it had no role in execution of the project. 
(C) Whether the ld. Lowers Courts are justified in not considering the issue about non joinder of Contractor as necessary party who was executing project and in possession of the site? 
(D) Whether the lower Courts are justified in holding that the deceased has passed away because of the accident though it is on record that he tried to avoid accident with NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined buffalo and lost his balance / control of two wheeler and fell down in pit.

3 (E) Whether the lower Courts are justified in holding the appellant responsible for payment of compensation though a Doctor as an expert had stated that there was no internal or exterior injury to the deceased and he passed away because of heart attack." 
6. It is well settled that Second Appeal under section 100 of CPC can only be entertained on substantial question of law. In H.P.Pyarejan v/s. Dasappa (Dead) by LRs [(2006)) 2 SCC 496],
Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under :-
"16. In our opinion, therefore, the judgment of the High Court suffers from serious infirmities. It suffers from the vice of exercise of jurisdiction which did not vest in the High Court under the law. Under Section 100 of the Code (as amended in 1976) the jurisdiction of the High Court to interfere with the judgments of the courts below is confined to hearing on substantial questions of law. Interference with finding of fact by the High Court is not warranted if it involves reappreciation of evidence (see Panchugopal Barua v. Umesh Chandra Goswami [(1997) 4 SCC 713] and Kshitish Chandra Purkait v. Santosh Kumar Purkait [(1997) 5 SCC 438] ). The High Court has not even discussed any evidence. No basic finding of fact recorded by the courts below has been reversed much less any reason assigned for taking a view contrary to that taken by the courts below. The finding on the question of readiness and willingness to perform the contract which is a mixed question of law and fact has been upset. It is statutorily provided by Section 16(1)(c) of the Act that to succeed in a suit for specific performance of a contract the plaintiff shall aver and prove that he has performed and has always been ready and willing to perform the essential terms of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined contract which were to be performed by him other than the terms the performance of which has been prevented or waived by the defendant." 
7. In yet another judgment in case of Ram Prasad Rajak v/s. Nand Kumar and Bros. and Another [(1998) 6 SCC 748], the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "Once the proceeding in the High Court is treated as a Second Appeal under Section 100 CPC, the restrictions prescribed in the said Section would come into play. The High Court could and ought to have dealt with the matter as a Second Appeal and found out whether a substantial question of law arose for consideration. Unless there was a substantial question of law, the High Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the Second Appeal and consider the merits." 
8. In Hero Vinoth v/s. Seshammal [(2006) 5 SCC 545], the Hon'ble Apex Court followed the judgment in the case of Sir Chunnilal V. Lal Mehta and Sons v/s. Century Spinning and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. [AIR 1962 SC 1314] and held as under :-
"21. The phrase "substantial question of law", as occurring in the amended Section 100 CPC is not defined in the Code. The word substantial, as qualifying "question of law", means of having substance, essential, real, of sound worth, important or 4 AIR 1962 SC 1314 5 AIR 1951 Mad 969 6 (2006) 5 SCC 545 considerable. It is to be Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
4 understood as something in contradistinction with technical, of no substance or consequence, or academic merely. However, it is clear that the legislature has chosen not to qualify the scope of "substantial question of law" by suffixing the words "of general importance" as has been done in many other provisions such as Section 109 of the Code or Article NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED:
09/09/2024 undefined 133(1)(a) of the Constitution. The substantial question of law on which a second appeal shall be heard need not necessarily be a substantial question of law of general importance. In Guran Ditta v. Ram Ditta [AIR 1928 PC 172] the phrase "substantial question of law" as it was employed in the last clause of the then existing Section 100 CPC (since omitted by the Amendment Act, 1973) came up for consideration and their Lordships held that it did not mean a substantial question of general importance but a substantial question of law which was involved in the case. In Sir Chunilal case [1962 Supp (3) SCR 549 : AIR 1962 SC 1314] the Constitution Bench expressed agreement with the following view taken by a Full Bench of the Madras High Court in Rimmalapudi Subba Rao v.
Noony Veeraju [AIR 1951 Mad 969 : (1951) 2 MLJ 222 (FB)] : (Sir Chunilal case [1962 Supp (3) SCR 549 : AIR 1962 SC 1314] , SCR p. 557) "[W]hen a question of law is fairly arguable, where there is room for difference of opinion on it or where the Court thought it necessary to deal with that question at some length and discuss alternative views, then the question would be a substantial question of law. On the other hand if the question was practically covered by the decision of the highest court or if the general principles to be applied in determining the question are well settled and the only question was of applying those principles to the particular fact of the case it would not be a substantial question of law."
9. In the case of Chandrabhan (Decesaed) through LRs v/s. Saraswati [2022 (13) Scale 777], the Hon'ble Apex Court in para- 33 has summarized principles relating to Second Appeal under section 100 of CPC as under :-
"33. The principles relating to Section 100 of the CPC relevant for this case may be summarised thus:
(i) An inference of fact from the recitals or contents of a document is a question of fact. But the legal effect of the terms of a document is a question of law. Construction of a NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined document involving the application of any principle of law, is also a question of law. 
Therefore, when there is misconstruction of a document or wrong application of a principle of law in construing a document, it gives rise to a question of law. 
(ii) The High Court should be satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law, and not a mere question of law. A question of law having a material bearing on the decision of the case (that is, a question, answer to which affects the rights of parties to the suit) will be a substantial question of law, if it is not covered by any specific provisions of law or settled legal principle emerging from binding precedents Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
5 and involves a debatable legal issue. A substantial question of law will also arise in a contrary situation, where the legal position is clear, either on account of express provisions of law or binding precedents, but the court below has decided the matter,
either ignoring or acting contrary to such legal principle. In the second type of cases,
the substantial question of law arises not because the law is still debatable, but because the decision rendered on a material question, violates the settled position of law. 
(iii) The general rule is that the High Court will not interfere with findings of facts arrived at by the courts below. But it is not an absolute rule. Some of the well- recognised exceptions are where (i) the courts below have ignored material evidence or acted on no evidence; (ii) the courts have drawn wrong inferences from proved facts by applying the law erroneously; or (iii) the courts have wrongly cast the burden of proof. When we refer to "decision based on no evidence", it not only refers to cases where there is a total dearth of evidence, but also refers to any case, where the evidence, taken as a whole, is not reasonably capable of supporting the finding."
10. In Second Appeal under section 100 of CPC in view of judgment of Chandrabhan (supra), three conditions have been recognized to disturb finding of facts viz. The courts below have ignored material evidence or acted on no evidence; (ii) the courts NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined have drawn wrong inferences from proved facts by applying the law erroneously; or (iii) the courts have wrongly cast the burden of proof. Thus,
decision based on no evidence, does not refer only to cases where there is a total dearth of evidence,
but also refers to case, where the evidence, taken as a whole, is not reasonably capable of supporting the finding. 
11. In background of above settled legal position, if we go through case on hand, it is undisputed that deceased died while he was going on his vehicle on 26.07.1992. When he was passing Shri Krishna Takies to Mochi Bazar Post Office, work of underground gutter was going on and workers /
employees of Rajkot Municipal Corporation or Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board had dug fifteen feet deep trenches and there were trench hillocks of soil dug on both sides of road. That all of sudden stray buffaloes rushed towards deceased and due to attack of buffaloes, deceased lost control and fell down and thereafter died while shifting him to Civil Hospital. Therefore, plaintiffs who are wife and daughters of deceased filed suit for compensation. 
12. Learned Trial Court framed following eight issues at Exh.31, they are as under :-
1.Whether plaintiffs prove that defendant is legally responsible to control the stray animals ?
2.whether plaintiffs prove that defendant no. 2 or the men NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined deployed by the contractor appointed by defendant no. 2 have dug 15 feet (ie. Equal to the height of three men)

6 deep pits (or trench) at the site of incident ?
3. Whether plaintiffs prove that the death of deceased Vrujlal was caused due to negligence and carelessness of defendants ?
4. Whether plaintiffs prove that the date of birth of deceased Vrujlal was dt.
16/08/1946 ? 
5. Whether plaintiffs prove that deceased was serving as pharmacist in the department of Kamadar Vima Joyana, Rajkot, of Government of Gujarat and he had monthly salary of Rs. 2877/- ? 
6. Whether plaintiffs prove that the present suit suffers from the non joinder of necessary party ? 
7. Whether plaintiffs are entitled for the relief prayed for ? 
8. What order and decree ? 
13. Issue no.1 to 5 are answered in affirmative, issue no.6 is partly answered in affirmative and issue no.7 is answered in negative. Learned Trial Court in para 7 to 10 has observed as under :-
" 7 . Issue no. 1 : Whether plaintiffs prove that defendant is legally responsible to control the stray animals ? It is argued by plaintiff that it is the responsibility of Rajkot Municipal Corporation to keep the public places like the place of incident free from 10/17 unhygienic surroundings and stray animal like buffaloes under the provisions NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporation Act ('BPMC Act' in short). 
Defendant corporation argued that it is not their responsibility to catch the stray animal and that it is the responsibility of police under the Bombay Police Act. 
Perusing the deposition given on behalf of defendant no. 1 Corporation, it appears that he has conceded the fact that the Municipal Corporation has the responsibility to control the stray animal on the roads and streets of city. He has also said that it is their discretionary duty. It is important here to refer as following the relevant provision of BPMC Act. 
Chapter VI : Duties and Powers of the Municipal Authorities and Officers xxx xxx Section 66 : Matters which may be provided for by Corporation at its discretion. 
xxx xxx (24) the destruction of birds or animals causing a nuisance, or of vermin, and the confinement or destruction of stray or ownerless dogs; It is the daily affair in our cities and towns that one invariably find stray animal like cows, buffaloes and dogs near the market places especially the vegetable markets. It is because of the said prevailing phenomena of hygiene, safety and propriety in public places in our cities Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
7 and towns that the above provision has been incorporated in the BPMC Act. The corporations are the institution of self government. Corporations raise taxes from the residents of cities so that the functions and duties can be funded and accomplished. It is also the responsibility of corporation to keep the city clean so that among other things the cows, buffaloes and dogs do not get to gather to search for trash food in garbage especially near vegetable markets. Thus, it can not be said that Municipal corporation does not owe any responsibility to control stray animal like buffalo on the streets and roads of city. The liability on police under the Bombay Police Act is a subject of Law and Order and related criminal responsibility of an individual. That the said responsibility of police in connection with preservation of Law and order can not be equated with that of the responsibility of Municipal Corporation which raises taxes from the people NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED:
09/09/2024 undefined unlike police. In light of these, the argument on defendant side that it is the responsibility of only police to control the 11/17 stray animal does not deserve to be accepted. It will therefore have to be inferred that Rajkot Municipal Corporation has the responsibility to control the stray animal. In this way, the issue no. 1 is answered in affirmative. 
8. Issue no. 2 : whether plaintiffs prove that defendant no.
2 or the men deployed by the contractor appointed by defendant no. 2 have dug 15 feet (ie. Equal to the height of three men) deep pits (or trench) at the site of incident ?
Both the defendants have averred or contended and also affirmed in their written statements that work of drainage in the area of 50 to 100 feet at the place of incident was in progress. That defendant no. 1 has been given a task of gutter and drainage. That the World Bank has given loan for the under ground gutter work. That the work of drainage and gutter has been given to defendant no.
2 by defendant no. 1. That the contract was allotted on behalf of defendant no. 1 to suitable contractor for doing the work of gutter and drainage. Defendants have chosen to deny the depth of trench as depicted in the present issue, but at the same time desisted from giving the actual information of exact depth of the trench. The information of actual depth of the trench for gutter dug at the place of incident is within the exclusive knowledge of defendants. It is a fact that the same is withheld and has not been provided in the present case by defendant no. 1 and 2. Therefore, it will have to be inferred applying the provisions of s. 114 (g) that the detail withheld if provided will be unfavorable to defendants which withheld it. Defendants have also contended and affirmed that soil dug from the trench is kept on the two sides of such trench as protection hedge or wall. This fact gives rise to a conclusion that trench dug was deep enough to keep a hillock of soil dug on two sides of trench for protection in order that a person or animal do not fall in to it and get injured. In addition to all these, perusing the panchnama produced by plaintiff at ex. 42, It appears that the trench is shown as measuring 15 feet NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED:
09/09/2024 undefined deep at the site of incident. Defendants have accepted that their men or men on their behalf have dug the trenches at the place of incident. Thus, it can be said and inferred that there were 15 feet deep pits or trenches at the place of incident and the same were dug by defendant no. 2 or its men. In this way, issue no. 2 is hereby answered in affirmative.

8 9. Issue no. 4 and 5 : 
4. Whether plaintiffs prove that the date of birth of deceased Vrujlal was dt.
16/08/1946 ?
5.Whether plaintiffs prove that deceased was serving as pharmacist in the department of Kamadar Vima Joyana, Rajkot, of Government of Gujarat and he had monthly salary of Rs. 2877/- ? 
Plaintiffs in their plaint has averred that date of birth of Vrujlal Popatlal Rathod was 16/8/1946. 
That the same has been affirmed by plaintiff in his deposition affidavit in oral evidence. In addition to all this, plaintiffs have produced the original school leaving certificate at ex. 39 of he deceased. In the said school leaving certificate issued by Karansinhji High School on dated 08/7/1975, the date of birth of deceased has been shown as dt. 16/8/1946. That the said date of birth has not been controverted by any cogent and reliable documentary or oral evidence by defendants. The only denial by defendants not supported by any cogent and reliable documentary and oral evidence can not be said to be sufficient in present case. Thus, plaintiff can be said to be successful in proving date 16/8/1946 as the the date of birth of deceased Vrujlal Popatlal Rathod. 
Plaintiffs have averred that deceased was serving as pharmacist in the department of Kamadar Vima Joyna, Rajkot, of Government of Gujarat and drawing monthly salary of Rs. 2,877/-. That the said fact has been denied by defendants. Plaintiff has affirmed the said fact of plaint in the deposition affidavit. Plaintiffs have also produced at ex. 40 salary sleep of deceased Vrujlal Popatlal duly NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined signed. Perusing the said salary sleep, it appears that it is of July, 1992 and gross salary is shown as Rs. 2,877/-. On the other hand, defendant except denial, have not produced any cogent and reliable oral as well as documentary evidence to controvert the said fact or suggest otherwise. The only denial by defendants not supported by any cogent and reliable documentary and oral evidence can not be said to be sufficient in present case. Thus, plaintiff can be said to be successful in proving the fact that the deceased was serving as pharmacist in the department of Kamadar Vima Joyana, Rajkot, of Government of Gujarat and he had monthly gross salary of Rs. 2877/-. In this way issue no. 4 and 5 are hereby answered in affirmative. 
10. Issue no. 3 : Whether plaintiffs prove that the death of deceased Vrujlal was caused due to negligence and carelessness of defendants ? 
It is the case of plaintiffs that deceased Vrujlal Popatlal Rathod was passing at the place of incident on the fateful day more particularly described in the plaint. That the trenches 15 feet deep were dug for sewage and there were hillocks of soil dug on the two sides of such trenches. That there is a vegetable market near to the place of incident. That vegetable vendors too keep their stalls at the sides of the road at the site of incident. That buffaloes suddenly rushed towards the deceased who had as result been caused sudden fear and tension resulting in to a heart attack. That his Luna Moped fell in the trench dug there. That in the hospital, deceased was declared as brought dead. It is also averred by plaintiffs that there was no sign board and strip enclosing the area where the digging Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
9 work was in progress. It is thus the allegation leveled by plaintiffs that it is because of negligence of defendants firstly, in not controlling the stray animal at the place of incident and secondly, in not putting any sign board or cautioning activity at the site that the incident of accident and resultant death due to shock owing to instant fear and tension occurred. Plaintiffs have therefore alleged that defendants are liable to pay the compensation for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined death of deceased for being negligent. 
Defendants have contended and argued that they were not responsible for the death of deceased, as he was a patient of heart disease and it may be a coincidence that he might have suffered a heart attack. In fact, deceased him self was negligent, as he was riding a moped at a place were there were trenches dug and hillocks of soil dug. That it was not safe to drive a moped at such place. It is also argued and contended that corporation is not responsible for controlling the stray animal (buffaloes) and that it is the police which is responsible for doing needful in case of stray animal under the provisions of Bombay Police Act. Defendant no. 2 has argued that if this court comes to a conclusion that compensation is awardable to plaintiffs, it is not responsible for paying compensation in view of condition no. 3 (f) of the contract between defendant no. 1 and 2 produced at ex. 85. A judgment below Second appeal no. 249/2010 delivered on dated 12/7/2011 by hon'ble Gujarat High Court (hon'ble Justice Ms. Harsha Devani) has also been shown by defendant no. 2 to canvass before the court that in case involving similar circumstances of contract between defendant no. 1 and 2, defendant no. 1 Municipal Corporation was held to be liable to pay compensation. 
Perusing the plaint, it is the case of plaintiff that on account of sudden rushing of buffaloes at the site of incident, deceased who was passing through the place of incident by his Luna Moped, could not run away to save him self due to trenches of sewage and hillocks of soil dug from the said trenches, fell down and was caused a heart attack because of sudden fear and tension. That the said fact has been affirmed by plaintiff in the deposition affidavit. Plaintiffs have also produced panchanama of the site of incident at ex. 42. In the said panchanama, it has been mentioned that there were trenches of sewage dug and there were hillocks off soil dug from these trenches of sewage. It is also mentioned that three four buffaloes came rushing towards the deceased and as a result deceased tried to run away keeping aside his Moped which fell in to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined the trench. There is no documentary or oral reliable and cogent evidence on defendant side to controvert the probability of the incident narrated in the plaint and mentioned in the panchanama of the incident. It is true and acdepted by the parties hereof that the place of incident is near to the vegetable market. That fruit and vegetable vendors throng the said place. It is the Mochi Bazar area and a very busy place of Rajkot. There is all probability that buffaloes were roaming around at the place to have free meal near the vegetable and fruit market. The buffaloes suddenly running at the site in such a place of commotion does appear probable and possible. As earlier held by this court hereinbefore that Municipal Corporation has a legal responsibility to control the stray animal like buffaloes. This court can take even a judicial notice that stray animal roam around on the city roads and place of jaunt freely to the extend that one may force to think that such animal has the fundamental right to roam around and create obstacle in our cities and towns. People seem to do nothing except to raise there voice for some days against the problem of stray animal and everything subsides thereafter without any result. Common people have resigned to the fact that something will be and can be done to solve the problem of stray Rajkot Municipal Corporation vs Bhanuben Vrajlal Rathod on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119280767/
10 animal roaming around on the street and roads of our cities and towns. Foreigners from the western countries take the photos of the stray animals sitting in the middle of road as souvenirs, as these sight is new and surprising for them. But for the residents of our cities and towns, it is as common as cold. Coming back to the place of incident, Defendants have accepted that trenches for sewage were dug and there were hillocks of soil dug from these trenches. It was the morning time on Sunday, it can not be said that there were no fruit and vegetable vendors in and around the place of incident where there is a vegetable market just round the corner. Neither it can be said that there were less number of people in the area of place of incident. Defendants have not said in their depositions that precautionary signs or strings were attached at the place of incident to caution the people passing by that there is danger ahead. In fact it was accepted by defendants that there was no sign board or string encircling the area of trench. In fact there is no evidence NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined produced by defendants that any precautionary steps of putting sign board or string encircling the area of trench and hillock were taken. In such a busy area, a person, nearing his retirement age confronted suddenly with few rushing buffaloes at a place where there are pits and trenches dug and there is commotion around, is at risk of his life. Plaintiff side produced one judgment viz. 2013 AIR SCW 283 Mst. Param Pal Singh through father v. National Insurance Company. In the said judgment, it has been held that stress and strain can cause heart attack. In the scenario described at the time and place of incident, it can be said that a person of the age of deceased would have definitely undergone grave strain and stress on account of deceased finding no place to run away due to trenches dug and hillocks of soil around due to fear of falling in trenches and getting injured grievously by rushing buffaloes towards him. 
Even if deceased is taken as one suffering from heart disease, it can be said that his ailment is aggravated by the manner in and place at which incident occurred.
